23-034.r: Council of States' exclusive powers → recommend creation of new All India Services and let Parliament legislate on a State List subject (Art 249); resolution by two-thirds present and voting.

23-035.r: Exclusive power of Rajya Sabha → creation of new All India Services (Art 312), by resolution of two-thirds of members present and voting.

23-036.r: Art 312(1): Rajya Sabha resolution in national interest, passed by two-thirds of members present and voting → Parliament may create new All India Services.
23-036.t: Two-thirds of members present and voting, NOT two-thirds of total membership.

23-037.r: Rajya Sabha has equal power with Lok Sabha in amending the Constitution (Art 368(2)): bill in either House, passed by each with special majority.
23-037.t: Not equal in removing the government or cut motions (Lok Sabha only); All India Services is a Rajya Sabha power.

23-038.r: Government defeated in Rajya Sabha → no resignation, dissolution or President's Rule; Council of Ministers is responsible only to Lok Sabha (Art 75(3)).

23-039.r: Fourth Schedule → allocates Rajya Sabha seats to States; 7th → Union-State powers; 8th → 22 languages; 5th and 6th → Scheduled Areas and Tribes.

23-040.r: Rajya Sabha: Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu had 18 seats each (before June 2014); now Andhra 11, Telangana 7; Maharashtra 19; Gujarat 11.

23-041.r: In 2000: UP's 34 Rajya Sabha seats = Andhra Pradesh 18 + Madhya Pradesh 16; now UP 31, Uttarakhand 3, Chhattisgarh 5, Andhra 11, Telangana 7.

23-042.r: Rajya Sabha seats (Fourth Schedule): Maharashtra 19; Tamil Nadu 18; Bihar 16; Karnataka 12.

23-043.r: Madhya Pradesh had 16 Rajya Sabha seats; Chhattisgarh got 5, so MP now has 11; Maharashtra 19, Tamil Nadu 18, West Bengal 16.

23-044.r: Rajya Sabha seats: Andhra Pradesh 18 (till June 2014; now 11, Telangana 7); Maharashtra 19; Karnataka 12; West Bengal 16.

23-045.r: Rajya Sabha seats: Punjab 07; Jharkhand 06; Chhattisgarh 05; Uttarakhand 03.

23-046.r: Rajya Sabha seats: Karnataka 12; Gujarat 11; Rajasthan 10; Punjab 7.

23-047.r: Rajya Sabha seats: Karnataka 12; Gujarat 11; Odisha 10; Kerala 9; Uttar Pradesh 31.

23-048.r: Rajya Sabha seats, decreasing: Karnataka 12 > Gujarat 11 > Odisha 10 > Kerala 9.

23-049.r: Wrong pair: Andhra Pradesh 18 → now 11 Rajya Sabha seats (7 went to Telangana); Odisha 10, Tamil Nadu 18, Maharashtra 19 are correct.

23-050.r: Fewest elected Rajya Sabha members among options → Himachal Pradesh (3); Jammu and Kashmir 4 (now UT), Chhattisgarh 5, Jharkhand 6.

23-051.r: Union Territories are represented in both Houses; Rajya Sabha: Delhi 3, Puducherry 1, Jammu and Kashmir 4.

23-052.r: Rajya Sabha Chairman (Vice-President) is not a member, but the Deputy Chairman is; nominated MPs vote in Vice-President's election, not in President's.
23-052.t: President: only elected MPs and MLAs vote; Vice-President: all MPs, elected and nominated.

23-053.r: Chairman of Rajya Sabha → Vice-President, ex officio (Arts 64, 89(1)); VP elected by members of both Houses of Parliament (Art 66(1)).

23-054.r: Vice-President → ex-officio Chairman of Rajya Sabha (Arts 64, 89(1)) but not a member of either House; an MP elected VP loses his seat.

23-055.r: House presided over by a non-member → Rajya Sabha (Chairman = Vice-President, elected by members of both Houses).

23-060.r: Rajya Sabha Chairman = Vice-President (ex officio); at question time → Hamid Ansari; now → C.P. Radhakrishnan.

23-061.r: Incorrect: S. Radhakrishnan not the only two-term Chairman; Hamid Ansari too (2007-2017); 1st Amendment (1951) predated Rajya Sabha; 8 UT members; 3 joint sittings.
23-061.h: Joint sittings 'D-B-P': Dowry (1962), Banking Service Commission Repeal (1978), Prevention of Terrorism (2002).

23-062.r: Rajya Sabha first constituted → 3 April 1952; maximum 250 (12 nominated), present 245; one-third retire every two years.

23-063.r: 2024 Rajya Sabha nominations by President Droupadi Murmu: Satnam Singh Sandhu (30 January) and Sudha Murty (8 March), the 12th nominated member.

23-064.r: Rajya Sabha member who can take part in Lok Sabha deliberations → a Minister (not an ordinary nominated member or the Deputy Chairman).

24-001.r: Lok Sabha (Art 81): up to 530 State members + up to 20 UT members (the 'X') + 2 Anglo-Indians earlier (ended 25 January 2020); Rajya Sabha: 250 (238 + 12).

24-002.r: Art 87 special address → President addresses both Houses of Parliament 'assembled together' (Constitution's words, not 'joint sitting').

24-003.r: Art 87(1): President addresses both Houses at the first session after each general election and the first session of each year; tells Parliament the causes of its summons.

24-004.r: Art 59(1) → President is not a member of either House; Art 79 → Parliament = President + two Houses; both are written in the Constitution.

24-005.r: President → integral part of Parliament (Parliament = President + Council of States + House of the People), though not a member and does not sit in it.

24-014.r: Not part of Parliament → Vice-President; Parliament = President + Council of States + House of the People (Art 79, Part V).

24-015.r: Parliament must meet at least twice a year; gap between two sessions cannot exceed six months (Art 85(1)).

24-017.r: Officers of Parliament → Lok Sabha Speaker, Deputy Speaker, Secretary-General of Lok Sabha and Chairman of Rajya Sabha.

24-018.r: MP absent from all meetings for 60 days without permission → House may declare seat vacant (Art 101(4)); prorogation/adjournment over four days not counted.

24-019.r: MP absent without permission from all meetings for sixty days (two months) → House may declare his seat vacant (Art 101(4)).

24-021.r: First MP disqualified for 60 days' absence → Barjinder Singh Hamdard, Independent Rajya Sabha member from Punjab, in 2000.

24-022.r: MP elected to a State Legislature must resign the State seat within 14 days, else his seat in Parliament becomes vacant (Art 101(2); 1950 rules).

24-023.r: Privilege motion against a Minister → when he withholds facts of a case or gives a distorted version of facts.

24-024.r: Office of profit bar on MPs → Article 102(1)(a): office under Union or State Government disqualifies, unless exempted by Parliament's law.

24-025.r: 'Office of profit' is not defined in the Constitution or RP Act, 1951; Parliament (Prevention of Disqualification) Act, 1959 exempts posts; amended five times.

24-026.r: Office of profit: declared by law by Parliament (Art 102(1)(a)) or State Legislature (Art 191(1)(a)); disqualification decided by President/Governor on Election Commission's advice (Arts 103, 192).
24-026.c: Book prints two answers, (a) and (b), each right under a different reading of the question.

24-027.r: Powers, privileges and immunities of Parliament, its members and committees → Article 105.

24-028.r: Collective privileges: freedom of debates, excluding strangers, regulating own procedure, punishing breach; freedom from attending as witness → an individual privilege.

24-029.r: Courts barred from inquiring into the proceedings of Parliament → Article 122.

24-030.r: Elected MLAs (State Lower House) → vote in Lok Sabha elections (as citizens), Rajya Sabha elections and the Presidential election.

24-031.r: Earlier, a Rajya Sabha candidate had to be a voter of that State; RP Act amended in 2003 removed this; Supreme Court upheld it in 2006.
